::: {#rem-time-hierarchy-general}
#### Proof and consequences of the time hierarchy theorem

A refinement of the proof of @thm-time-hierarchy proves @thm-time-hierarchy-general.
It uses the same diagonal machine,
but with a clock that costs a constant number of steps per simulated step on average,
in place of the $\asymub{\log_2 n}$ steps per subtraction in the proof of @thm-time-hierarchy.
That proof could afford the extra $\log_2 n$ factor only
because $n^{1.4}$ and $n^{1.5}$ differ by a power of $n$.
The $\log_2 f(n)$ factor in the hypothesis is the overhead of the universal machine
in [the universal machine theorem](models-of-computation.qmd#thm-universal-tm).
Since $n^c \log_2 n^c = o(n^{c + 1})$,
$\text{DTIME}(n^c)$ is a proper subset of $\text{DTIME}(n^{c + 1})$ for every integer $c \ge 1$,
so [the class P](p-and-np.qmd#def-class-p) is not equal to $\text{DTIME}(n^c)$ for any single constant $c$.

:::
